purpose: Explain to citizens when and why an approved property answer changes, is corrected or is superseded, preserving the previous snapshot and distinguishing evidence changes, legal changes, procedural changes and corrections.
core_principle: OLD ANSWER → MATERIAL CHANGE → WHY → NEW EVIDENCE/LAW → NEW ANSWER → WHAT STAYS THE SAME → NEXT
rules: A new source does not automatically mean the previous answer was wrong.
A corrected property match can change a property-specific answer without changing general law.
Evidence changes and legal-rule changes are described separately.
Historical answers remain anchored to their historical date and legal version.
A procedure or deadline change may alter the next action without changing the substantive property answer.
A material correction creates a new snapshot while preserving the previous snapshot.
The reason for change must be supported by the recorded change and affected dependency.
Unresolved cause of a change is stated rather than invented.
Unchanged components remain visible so the citizen can see the actual scope of the revision.
No internal confidence score, chain-of-thought or restricted evidence is exposed.
hard_stops: Never silently overwrite a published answer.
Never invent why an answer changed.
Never confuse a source update with a legal change.
Never use current law to rewrite a historical answer without temporal authority.
Never call new evidence decisive unless its effect has been established.
Never remove the previous snapshot from the audit chain.
